o: The apostle's joy and praise for Philemon's steady faith in the Lord Jesus, and love to all the saints.
He recommends Onesimus as one who would make rich amends for the misconduct of which he had been guilty; and on behalf of whom the apostle promises to make up any loss Philemon had sustained.
bg: Was written from Rome at the same time as the epistles to the Colossians and Ephesians, and was sent also by Onesimus. It was addressed to Philemon and the members of his family.
(small, little). Nearly all the original materials for the life St. Paul are contained in the Acts of the Apostles and in the Pauline epistles.
An inhabitant of Colosse, and apparently a person of some note among the citizens (Col. 4:9; Philemon 1:2). He was brought to a knowledge of the gospel through the instrumentality of Paul

Useful, a slave who, after robbing his master Philemon (q.v.) at Colosse, fled to Rome, where he was converted by the apostle Paul, who sent him back to his master with the epistle which bears his name. In it he beseeches Philemon to receive his slave as a "faithful and beloved brother."
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle's joy and praise for Philemon's steady faith in the Lord Jesus, and love to all the saints (vv. 1–7); He recommends Onesimus as one who would make rich amends for the misconduct of which he had been guilty; and on behalf of whom the apostle promises to make up any loss Philemon had sustained (vv. 8–22); Salutations and a blessing (vv. 23–25). People named: Paul, Philemon, Onesimus, Apphia, Archippus, Epaphras.
ch.mh: Faith in Christ, and love to him, should unite saints more closely than any outward relation can unite the people of the world.
q: Read verses 1–7 (The apostle's joy and praise for Philemon's steady faith in the Lord Jesus, and love to all the saints). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?

In verses 8–22 (He recommends Onesimus as one who would make rich amends for the misconduct of which he had been guilty; and on behalf of whom the apostle promises to make up any loss Philemon had sustained), what do you learn about faith and trust?
Verse 6 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside 2 Peter 1:8. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Paul’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of the church and fellowship in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Philemon?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us do that now, which we should do at the last breath.
ch.a: Name one worry and deliberately hand it over to God in prayer each day this week.
